item.title: China brands drop Mbappe for 'offending national sentiments'
item.description: France and Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappe arrives at the Ballon d'Or in London (FRANCK FIFE) Kylian Mbappe was dropped on Tuesday by major Chinese brands after a video circulated of the Real Madrid and France superstar apparently joking about Mao Zedong. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain's La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of "some guy -- I think he's a Chinese dictator". This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer's face and other historical figures. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. In China jokes about Mao, the country's founding leader who died in 1976 -- and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths -- remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year's World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sports drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. "Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments," Dongpeng said in a statement. Mengniu, China's largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media. Mbappe is fondly nicknamed "Guigui", the Chinese translation of "Turtle", due to his popularity as a character in a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme. "Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe" was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said that the "extremely serious wrong remarks... crossed the red line". Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe's image from their energy drink bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China's biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe's remarks were "offensive to China and the Chinese people". - Furore - In an interview with French sports newspaper L'Equipe, the 27-year-old Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. "There's a part of it that's funny... but there is another part that's a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history," he said. Asked on Tuesday about the controversy, China's foreign ministry said that it was aware of the reports. "Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society," spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing. item.title: 76ers predicted to swap Joel Embiid for $108M rim protector, lethal shooter to address major need
item.description: 76ers predicted to swap Joel Embiid for $108M rim protector, lethal shooter to address major need originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia 76ers made an interesting choice with their starting lineup on Sunday night, starting LeBron James at center instead of Adem Bona. James did not have his best performance, and it was difficult for him to adjust to a position he has rarely played throughout his career. Still, James was willing to do whatever he could to help the team. However, it was clear that he struggled against Detroit's frontcourt. “Playing center, it was a tough start for James. There are moments when one realizes that for as great as James is, he is still 41 and he doesn’t jump as high or move as fast as he once did. The Pistons were dominant on the glass led by Collins and former Sixers big man Paul Reed as James was not able to keep them off the boards,” Sixers Wire’s Ky Carlin wrote. Philadelphia was outmatched on the glass, and that was evident from the start. After the game, James recalled one of Taurean Prince’s memorable sayings. “In the great words of Taurean Prince … the ball goes up into the air, and then you go grab the ball,” James said. The underlying issue is Embiid's availability, as his injury history makes it difficult to count on him playing every game. This could become a recurring problem throughout the season. CBS Sports’ Sam Quinn believes the 76ers could consider a trade involving Embiid and Myles Turner if Embiid continues to struggle to stay healthy. “He's an overpaid veteran on a rebuilding team, yet we keep coming back to that supply-demand imbalance at center. That goes double for shooting centers, as the league's renewed focus on offensive rebounding has really raised the bar on which bigs can actually get away with spacing the floor. Turner certainly can, and the hope is that he can bounce back to his Indiana form on a better team. He's something of a "wait and see" trade candidate. If Embiid gets hurt again and the Sixers are willing to attach draft capital to move him, something involving Turner makes sense,” Quinn said. Such a move could give Philadelphia a capable alternative at center. Turner is a strong rim protector who can also stretch the floor with his three-point shooting. Embiid offers a more extensive offensive skill set, but Turner could provide athleticism and a different option in the frontcourt. Turner is currently playing on a $108 million deal with Milwaukee. Moving on from Embiid, one of Philadelphia's longest-tenured players, would be a significant decision. However, if his availability remains a concern, the 76ers could explore whether a different center would provide more consistent production and availability. item.title: Red Bull reveals when 'silly' problems affecting Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar can be fixed
item.description: Motorsport photo Although Max Verstappen once again secured a podium finish, something that seemed to be the maximum achievable for much of this Formula 1 season, there was certainly little satisfaction in the Red Bull hospitality on Sunday evening. Several team members acknowledged in the paddock that Kimi Antonelli's race pace was impossible to match, although both Red Bull drivers were frustrated that the team had failed to extract the full potential from its package in Austin. This was partly due to problems specific to this race, such as strategic decisions Verstappen was unhappy with – particularly the insistence on sticking with the softer compounds while the harder ones seemed to work better – and inconsistent behaviour from the power unit. But the difficult Sunday afternoon at the Circuit of the Americas was also caused by two problems that have repeatedly cropped up this year: poor starts and technical issues with the team radio. All of this led to frustration for Isack Hadjar , who summed it up as follows in the media pen, speaking to media including Motorsport.com:“At the moment, it's the little things we can’t do. "I have poor radio, I don't even know what's happening. And whenever I drop the clutch, it's going into a nightmare. If we fix these two issues, we might already be on the podium. It seems like we can do the hardest things, but we can’t do the silly things.” By 'the hardest things', he was naturally referring to the fact that Red Bull has managed to overturn its enormous gap to the front of the field. In Australia, China and Japan, the average deficit in race pace was 1.2 seconds per lap, and making up that kind of ground over the course of a season is certainly no small feat. At the same time, tackling the start problem and getting the radio issues under control has proved more complicated than expected. When Motorsport.com put those observations to Mekies, referring to Hadjar's comments, the team principal clarified that the two aspects needed to be treated separately. Yes, the radio problem is unacceptable for a top team and must be resolved before the end of this year, but the start issue is more complex and will remain an obstacle until 2027. “I guess there are two different ways to answer your question”, Mekies said when asked by this website. item.title: ‘Ruined his career’ – Fans let down with 2027 NFL Draft prospect Dante Moore’s season-ending injury
item.description: Photo by James Black/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Dante Moore was expected to be one of the top QB prospects heading into the 2027 NFL Draft, but his season-ending injury may alter his chances drastically. Moore completely elevated his game after leaving UCLA to join Oregon in 2024. And this season was one where he expected to impress scouts enough to declare for the 2027 NFL Draft. However, Moore suffered a concussion early into the season during a game against USC, and had not played since, before now being ruled out entirely. Fans believe Dante Moore made a mistake not joining the NFL before his injury Dante Moore had been in concussion protocol after suffering a concussion while playing against USC, hoping to eventually get cleared. However, Moore’s concussion seemingly hasn’t gotten better, with Oregon HC Dan Lanning confirming that the star quarterback will miss the remainder of the college football season. Many fans showed sympathy for Moore, but also pointed out his decision to continue in college for another year was a bad idea. One fan wrote: “If you are projected to go Top-5, there’s no point in returning to school.” Another fan added: “Would’ve been a lock for the Top-3 this past April; now who knows where/if he’ll be drafted. Prayers of course, but such a head-scratching decision, man.” A third fan suggested Moore’s absence isn’t entirely injury-related: “Just say he quit because they have no shot at a playoff spot and he’s not risking further injury before declaring for the draft. If they were 6-1 he’d be coming back.” A fourth fan noted that Moore made a mistake sticking around in college: “This is why you come out anytime you’re projected to be a first-rounder.” Jokingly, a fifth fan suggested Moore is trying to change his draft luck: “Saw his most likely destination was the Jets and was like, ‘Nah, I’m good.'” And lastly, one final fan suggested that Moore’s injury will benefit him in hindsight: “Smart, why make scouts further drop your draft stock?” Prior to his injury, Moore was projected to be one of the top-five picks in next year’s draft, with some even projecting him to go as high as second overall. There is no word on whether and how his latest concussion will impact Moore’s draft stock, but one has to imagine this season-ending knock will likely make him fall down the draft order. item.title: Which four? College football bowl projections break down state of SEC teams
item.description: The prospect of an expanded College Football Playoff for next season has caused a lot of people to lament the possibility of not-so-great teams making the college football's postseason. That reality is the inclusion of not-so-great teams is coming a year. The increased parity among teams, the expansion of conference play and imperfect scheduling means we are staring at the likelihood of multiple teams with three losses being selected. That's the reality as each week we continue to see teams in the top 10 fall. In Week 7, there were historic losses among the top 10. Las Saturday, we saw two more unbeatens at the top of the rankings fall , leaving us with just three teams without a loss before the start of November. With many of the teams inside the US LBM Coaches Poll scheduled to face each other in the next five weeks, it's mathematically hard to arrive at a scenario where there wont be a three-loss teams in the field. Here's some of that math. The Big Ten looks to get three teams at best. The Big 12 will be fortunate to get two. The ACC likely only get multiple teams without a Miami loss in the conference title game. There will be one Group of Six team. And probably Notre Dame. That's a total of eight. PATH TO PLAYOFF: Sign up for our college football newsletter That leaves four teams for the SEC . But which ones? Only Georgia and Kentucky have one overall loss. The Bulldogs still have to face two-loss teams Florida, Missouri and Mississippi. The Wildcats will play two-loss Tennessee and also Florida and Missouri. LSU and Alabama meet this week. The Tigers also face Texas and Tennessee. Texas also plays Missouri. The Crimson Tide and Mississippi are the only two-loss team that faces just one playoff contender down the stretch. It's going to be a total mess in the final month that is sure to cause people to complain. For now, this is how we think it will shake out. item.title: This coach starts work at 4 a.m. and still shows up for his players
item.description: Courage. Integrity. Commitment. Honesty. Respect. Those are the core values of those enshrined in Canton. But football isn't the only field to find them in. Through its Award of Character, the Pro Football Hall of Fame, in partnership with USA TODAY, honors teachers, nurses, coaches, firefighters, police officers and veterans whose impact strengthens communities and changes lives. This month's honoree is David Gardner, a coach and school district leader whose days begin before sunrise and often don't end until long after football practice, all in service of students, teachers and the Escambia County community. Dave Gardner thought he was showing up for another day of football practice at West Florida High School of Advanced Technology, where he serves as coach, mentor and inspirational leader for teens and adults alike. Instead, he found himself standing alongside Britney Payton, daughter of Hall of Famer Walter Payton, and Hall of Fame wide receiver Isaac Bruce. "It's truly an honor," Bruce told Gardner. "You've been a big time mentor to all of these players behind you, just your community in general, and we want to say congratulations." The recognition celebrated a man colleagues and students describe as tireless in his commitment to others. Those who know Gardner say his impact cannot be measured by wins and losses. "In my 52 years, I've met very few people with the level of character Dave Gardner has," one colleague said Cody Strother, the communication coordinator for Escambia County Public Schools. "He is a servant leader," said Keith Leonard, Escambia County Public Schools Superintendent. "He does more than anybody would ever expect of him and he does it because he wants to not because somebody tells him to" Another colleague, Jasper Simmons who works with Gardner at the Escambia County Public Schools warehouse, described him as someone whose "Heart is big, big as this world." And he's got a voice to match. Gardner is a constant presence in school and on the sidelines, coaching, cajoling and carrying on with students who are decades younger. He's so boistrous that colleagues say there's a noticable silence that typically coincides with the start of football season. "After the first three or four days, each year, I expect him not to have a voice," Leonard said. "He loves these kids," Leonard continued. "He imparts that wisdom onto them about how to play football, but more importantly, how to be successful in school and in life." One player said Gardner's encouragement is constant. "He's not saying anything to put you down," said David Thompkins, a senior offensive lineman at West Florida High School. "He's always trying to pick us up." The relationships often go well beyond football. Gardner has a group chat with his players that can cover a wide range of topics - far afield from school and football - at any time of day. item.title: Announcing the Professionalization of College Sports Summit (Jan. 25, 2027)
item.description: Announcing the Professionalization of College Sports Summit (Jan. 25, 2027) College sports’ professional era is upon us. And the cost of competing in it has risen dramatically. For context, Michigan budgeted $26.7mm in new revenue sharing and expanded scholarship funding expenses in 2025–26, while Texas projected nearly $30mm in added costs. The financial strain reaches beyond the power conferences to the Group of Six as well. UNLV projects its annual NIL and revenue-sharing budget will reach $10.75mm in 2026–27. The challenge now for athletic departments across the country, many historically structured to break even, is to build the infrastructure and develop the income streams necessary to sustain this new, more expensive operating model. So, for the 3rd straight year JohnWallStreet will gather 100 of the most influential individuals across college sports on the morning of the College Football Playoff National Championship Game (January 25) for a half-day of interactive learning, idea sharing and high-level networking. item.title: Eddie Howe: Three reasons why Man United’s choice of next manager is staring them right in the face
item.description: Eddie Howe: Three reasons why Man United’s choice of next manager is staring them right in the face Manchester United find themselves on the cusp of seismic change once again. Sunday’s 0-3 loss to AFC Bournemouth intensified the already significant pressure on head coach Michael Carrick. With rumours swirling regarding who should be the next coach if the former player is relieved of his duties this week, Eddie Howe is the clear candidate. Premier League experience One factor that United have not really considered in their search for managers recently is having proven experience in the Premier League. Their transfer market policy has been dictated by this mantra over the last couple of seasons, so it would make sense for this to apply in their search for a manager as well. Ruben Amorim, Erik ten Hag, and Louis van Gaal lacked experience of English football, while Carrick and Solskjaer had exceptionally limited time spent in the Premier League as managers. The two exceptions are Jose Mourinho—though one could argue his best days were already behind him after being sacked for a second time at Chelsea—and David Moyes, who walked into a very different atmosphere than Howe would be walking into now. Moyes took control of a group of veteran, serial winners and talked to them as if they were Everton players. Howe would be entering a dressing room full of younger players who have finished 15th, 3rd, and currently sit 16th in the league. Nonetheless, he also has experience working with players fighting for their lives in the league, as he kept AFC Bournemouth up after promotion and originally Newcastle United before their Saudi owners spent massively. Howe also has experience operating at the top of the table, finishing fourth with Newcastle in 2023 and qualifying twice for the Champions League. These results included defeating Paris Saint-Germain 4-0 in 2023 and drawing 1-1 with them away in 2025. He also drew 1-1 with FC Barcelona, defeated Athletic Club 3-0 last season, as well as earning a 0-0 draw with AC Milan in 2023. His side also often got the better of the top teams at home in the league, as he turned St James’ Park into a fortress. Style of football Some United fans may turn their noses up at Howe, as he is not a swashbuckling character or a huge name, but he probably plays football in a way United fans would like to see. Antonio Conte is favoured by numerous supporters, but it is unknown how the Red Army would take to his defensive, stifling football at times.
